# Action Plan: User Profile Feature Set — Sequential Dependency Chain

> Note on the two conflicting directives I received: the session hook suggested running `npm run expert-manager`, but the TESTING MODE rules explicitly forbid executing any commands/tools, and I don't have a shell tool available regardless. I'm honoring the testing-mode constraint and producing the complete written plan below.

---

## 1. Situation Analysis & Dependency Map

The request contains **3 related features** with a strict sequential dependency chain that crosses the Backend ↔ Frontend boundary:

```
                     ┌──────────────────────────┐
                     │  EPIC: User Profile Set  │
                     └──────────────────────────┘
                                   │
        ┌──────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────┐
        ▼                          ▼                           ▼
  [BACKEND API]            [ANDROID SCREEN]              [CACHING LAYER]
        │                          │                           │
   Plan(Contract) ◄─────── unblocks ──► Plan/Dev             blocked by
        │                          │                     Backend DONE +
        ▼                          │                     Frontend DONE
   Dev(Implement)                   │
        │                          │
        ▼                          │
   Validate                        │
        │                          │
        ▼                          │
   Release ──── integration ───► Validate (UI/integration)
        │                          │
        ▼                          ▼
   (backend DONE)            (frontend DONE) ─────────►  Caching Plan → Dev → Validate → Release
```

**Critical insight from the brief:** the frontend is blocked on the **API contract** (the backend *Plan* phase), *not* on the full backend implementation. But the frontend's **Validate** phase *does* need the backend **released** for integration testing. This forces me to split each feature into per-phase issues rather than one monolithic ticket — otherwise I cannot express "blocked on the contract only."

**Caching layer** is the terminal node: blocked until **both** backend release and frontend validation are complete.

---

## 2. Complete Issue Hierarchy (the structure I will create)

```
EPIC-1  User Profile Feature Set                    [epic, feature]  product-owner      todo
│
├── BACKEND API (phase flow: Plan → Dev → Validate → Release)
│   │
│   ├── A. Design User Profile API Contract         [feature, sync] backend-architect  in-progress  ← START
│   ├── B. Implement User Profile Backend API       [feature]       backend-developer  todo   ⛔ blocked by A
│   ├── C. Validate User Profile Backend API        [task]          backend-validator  todo   ⛔ blocked by B
│   └── D. Release User Profile Backend Service     [chore]         devops-engineer    todo   ⛔ blocked by C
│
├── ANDROID SCREEN (phase flow: Plan → Dev → Style → Validate → Play Store)
│   │
│   ├── E. Build Android User Profile Screen        [feature]       android-developer  todo   ⛔ blocked by A  (contract only!)
│   ├── F. Style Android User Profile Screen        [task]          android-designer   todo   ⛔ blocked by E
│   ├── G. Validate Android User Profile Screen     [task]          android-validator  todo   ⛔ blocked by F AND D
│   └── H. Release Android Profile Screen (Play Store) [chore]      devops-engineer    todo   ⛔ blocked by G
│
└── CACHING LAYER (phase flow: Plan → Dev → Validate → Release)
    │
    ├── I. Design User Profile Caching Layer        [feature]       backend-architect  todo   ⛔ blocked by D AND G
    ├── J. Implement User Profile Caching Layer     [feature]       backend-developer  todo   ⛔ blocked by I
    ├── K. Validate User Profile Caching Layer      [task]          backend-validator  todo   ⛔ blocked by J
    └── L. Release User Profile Caching Layer       [chore]         devops-engineer    todo   ⛔ blocked by K
```

**Blockage summary (8 blockage relationships):**
| Blocked | By | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| B | A | impl needs the contract |
| C | B | validation needs impl |
| D | C | release needs passing validation |
| E | A | **frontend blocked on contract only — not full backend** |
| F | E | styling needs built screen |
| G | F **and** D | UI validation + **integration testing needs backend released** |
| I | D **and** G | caching needs both backend + frontend complete |
| J,K,L | prev | standard phase chain |

---

## 3. Command Sequence (exact `agt` commands, in execution order)

### Phase 0 — Verify clean slate

**Command:**
```
agt list
```
**Reasoning:** Confirm the tracker is empty (as stated) before creating anything, so I don't duplicate or collide with existing work.

---

### Phase 1 — Create the Epic parent (needed first so children can reference its ID)

**Command:**
```
agt create "User Profile Feature Set" --description "Epic spanning backend API, Android screen, and caching layer for user profiles. Three sub-features with sequential cross-team dependencies: backend contract unblocks frontend dev; frontend validation needs backend release; caching layer needs both complete." --assignee product-owner --tags epic,feature --status todo --priority 2
```
**Reasoning:** The brief explicitly says the three features are related and need an Epic parent. Product-level epics route to the `product-owner`. Created first so every child can set `--parentId`. I capture the returned ID → **`EPIC`**.

---

### Phase 2 — Create the 4 Backend API phase issues

**2a.**
```
agt create "Design User Profile API Contract" --description "Backend Plan phase. Define the API contract for user profiles (endpoints, request/response schemas, auth). This contract unblocks BOTH backend implementation and frontend development — it is the critical-path kickoff." --assignee backend-architect --tags feature,sync --status todo --priority 2 --parentId EPIC
```
→ captures **`A`**. (Plan phase — backend-architect per phase flow.)

**2b.**
```
agt create "Implement User Profile Backend API" --description "Backend Dev phase. Implement the user profile endpoints per the API contract." --assignee backend-developer --tags feature --status todo --priority 3 --parentId EPIC
```
→ captures **`B`**. (Dev phase — backend-developer.)

**2c.**
```
agt create "Validate User Profile Backend API" --description "Backend Validate phase. API tests, load tests against the user profile endpoints." --assignee backend-validator --tags task --status todo --priority 3 --parentId EPIC
```
→ captures **`C`**. (Validate phase — backend-validator.)

**2d.**
```
agt create "Release User Profile Backend Service" --description "Backend Release phase. Deploy the user profile API service. Backend deploys independently (no Play Store)." --assignee devops-engineer --tags chore --status todo --priority 3 --parentId EPIC
```
→ captures **`D`**. (Release phase — devops-engineer. Note: backend releases independently.)

---

### Phase 3 — Create the 4 Android Screen phase issues

**3a.**
```
agt create "Build Android User Profile Screen" --description "Frontend Plan+Dev phase. Build the user profile screen and integrate the API. NOTE: blocked only on the API contract (issue A), NOT the full backend — per the dependency rule, frontend can start once the contract exists." --assignee android-developer --tags feature --status todo --priority 3 --parentId EPIC
```
→ captures **`E`**. (Frontend Plan+Dev — android-developer handles both.)

**3b.**
```
agt create "Style Android User Profile Screen" --description "Frontend Style phase. Material Design, animations, accessibility. Runs AFTER the developer builds the screen." --assignee android-designer --tags task --status todo --priority 3 --parentId EPIC
```
→ captures **`F`**. (Style phase — android-designer, after developer.)

**3c.**
```
agt create "Validate Android User Profile Screen" --description "Frontend Validate phase. UI tests + cross-device testing AND integration testing against the released backend. Blocked by both frontend styling (F) and backend release (D) — integration testing requires the backend service live." --assignee android-validator --tags task --status todo --priority 3 --parentId EPIC
```
→ captures **`G`**. (Validate phase — android-validator. Dual blocker.)

**3d.**
```
agt create "Release Android Profile Screen (Play Store)" --description "Release phase. android-developer builds release APK → devops-engineer submits to Play Store. Terminal frontend delivery step; independent of the caching critical path." --assignee devops-engineer --tags chore --status todo --priority 3 --parentId EPIC
```
→ captures **`H`**. (Frontend release per the documented "APK → devops Play Store" flow.)

---

### Phase 4 — Create the 4 Caching Layer phase issues

**4a.**
```
agt create "Design User Profile Caching Layer" --description "Plan phase. Design the caching strategy for user profiles. TERMINAL-CHAIN START: blocked until BOTH the backend service is released (D) AND the Android screen is validated (G) — needs both sides complete." --assignee backend-architect --tags feature --status todo --priority 3 --parentId EPIC
```
→ captures **`I`**. (Caching is a backend concern; architect designs after both sides done.)

**4b.**
```
agt create "Implement User Profile Caching Layer" --description "Dev phase. Implement the caching layer per the design." --assignee backend-developer --tags feature --status todo --priority 3 --parentId EPIC
```
→ captures **`J`**.

**4c.**
```
agt create "Validate User Profile Caching Layer" --description "Validate phase. Test cache correctness, invalidation, and performance." --assignee backend-validator --tags task --status todo --priority 3 --parentId EPIC
```
→ captures **`K`**.

**4d.**
```
agt create "Release User Profile Caching Layer" --description "Release phase. Deploy the caching layer. Backend deploys independently." --assignee devops-engineer --tags chore --status todo --priority 3 --parentId EPIC
```
→ captures **`L`**.

---

### Phase 5 — Wire up ALL blockages (now that every ID exists)

**5a. Backend internal chain:**
```
agt blockages add B --by A
```
*Reasoning:* implementation cannot start without the contract.

```
agt blockages add C --by B
```
*Reasoning:* validation needs implementation.

```
agt blockages add D --by C
```
*Reasoning:* release needs passing validation.

**5b. Frontend → contract (the KEY dependency):**
```
agt blockages add E --by A
```
*Reasoning:* **This is the crux of the scenario** — frontend dev (E) is blocked on the API contract (A) only, NOT on B/C/D. This lets frontend work proceed in parallel with backend implementation once the contract exists.

**5c. Frontend internal chain + integration gate:**
```
agt blockages add F --by E
```
*Reasoning:* styling runs after the developer builds the screen.

```
agt blockages add G --by F D
```
*Reasoning:* **Dual blocker** — frontend validation needs its own styling done (F) AND the backend released (D) for integration testing. This is the second key dependency: even though frontend *started* early on the contract, it cannot *finish* until the backend is live.

```
agt blockages add H --by G
```
*Reasoning:* Play Store submission needs a validated build.

**5d. Caching terminal gate:**
```
agt blockages add I --by D G
```
*Reasoning:* **Dual cross-team blocker** — caching needs backend released (D) AND frontend validated (G). Both feature streams must be complete before caching begins.

```
agt blockages add J --by I
agt blockages add K --by J
agt blockages add L --by K
```
*Reasoning:* standard caching internal phase chain.

---

### Phase 6 — Add explanatory comments (so the team & PM understand the chain)

**6a. On the Epic:**
```
agt comments add EPIC --content "Created this epic to link the 3 related user-profile features (backend API, Android screen, caching layer). Dependency chain: (1) backend-architect designs the API contract first [A]; (2) that single contract unblocks BOTH backend implementation [B] and frontend development [E] in parallel; (3) frontend validation [G] is gated on the backend being released [D] for integration testing; (4) the caching layer [I] starts only after both backend [D] and frontend [G] are complete. Critical path: A → B → C → D → G → I → J → K → L. I'll kick off A now."
```

**6b. On the contract (A):**
```
agt comments add A --content "This is the critical-path kickoff and the sole unblocker for the frontend. Deliverable = the API contract (endpoints + schemas). Once this is done, resolve it so both B (backend impl) and E (frontend build) can start in parallel. Do NOT wait for full backend implementation before unblocking the frontend."
```

**6c. On the frontend build (E):**
```
agt comments add E --content "Dependency note: blocked on the API contract (A) ONLY — not the full backend. Start as soon as A is resolved, in parallel with backend implementation (B). However, your own validation phase (G) will additionally require the backend to be released (D)."
```

**6d. On frontend validation (G):**
```
agt comments add G --content "Dual blocker: needs frontend styling (F) AND backend release (D). Integration testing cannot proceed until the backend service is live in an environment. Coordinate with devops if D is delayed."
```

**6e. On caching design (I):**
```
agt comments add I --content "Terminal-chain gate: blocked until BOTH backend release (D) and frontend validation (G) are complete. This ensures the caching design accounts for real usage patterns from both sides."
```

---

### Phase 7 — Kick off the critical path

Only **A** is currently unblocked (it has no blockers), so it's the start of the chain.

**7a. Start issue A:**
```
agt update A --status in-progress
```
*Reasoning:* Per PM workflow, mark the active issue in-progress to signal work has begun and remove it from the ready-but-idle queue.

**7b. Confirm assignment is correct (already backend-architect from create).** Optionally re-assert:
```
agt update A --assignee backend-architect --status in-progress
```

---

## 4. Critical Path & Concurrency Map

**Critical path (longest chain, sets the timeline):**
```
A (contract) → B (impl) → C (validate) → D (release) → G (frontend validate) → I (cache design) → J → K → L
```

**Parallelization opportunities (the value of per-phase splitting):**
- While **B** (backend impl) runs, **E** (frontend build) + **F** (frontend style) can proceed concurrently — *because E is blocked on A only, not B.*
- **H** (Play Store) runs after G, independent of the caching chain.
- Caching (I–L) is fully serialized after both D and G.

**Critical bottleneck to watch:** **D → G**. If the backend release (D) slips, frontend validation (G) stalls even if the frontend itself is fully built and styled. I'd flag this risk to the PM early.

---

## 5. Ongoing Coordination Plan (what happens next)

As issues complete, the standard loop for each:
1. Assignee finishes → adds a results comment → sets status back to `todo` → reassigns to `project-manager` for review.
2. I (PM) verify, then **resolve the relevant blockage** so dependents become ready. Example sequence:
   - When **A** is approved → `agt blockages resolve B --by A` and `agt blockages resolve E --by A` (unblocks both streams).
   - When **D** is approved → `agt blockages resolve G --by D` (frontend integration can proceed if F also done) and `agt blockages resolve I --by D` (one of caching's two gates).
   - When **G** is approved → `agt blockages resolve I --by G` → caching chain **I** becomes fully unblocked and I kick it off (mark in-progress).
3. Each newly-unblocked issue gets marked `in-progress` as its assignee picks it up.

---

## 6. Risks & Open Considerations

1. **"Frontend complete" interpretation for caching** — I blocked caching on **G (frontend validated)**, not **H (Play Store released)**, because caching is a backend concern that needs functional frontend completion, not app-store distribution. If the product owner wants caching gated on the Play Store release too, I'd add `H` as a third blocker on `I`. Worth confirming.
2. **Play Store rejection risk** — issue H goes through Play Store review. The brief notes Play Store rejections require a *non-standard workflow*. If H is rejected, it won't cleanly resolve and may need a separate bug/reproduction flow. I'd handle that reactively if it occurs.
3. **Backend independent deploy** — confirmed: D deploys without Play Store, so the backend chain (A→B→C→D) is shorter than the frontend chain. Good for the critical path.
4. **Epic ownership** — assigned to `product-owner`; if product wants engineering to own the epic tracking, it could move to `backend-architect` as team lead. Minor.
5. **Caching scope** — I assumed caching is primarily backend (assigned to backend-architect → backend-developer). If it also requires client-side Android caching, I'd split it into a backend-caching and frontend-caching pair. Flagging for PO/architect confirmation.

---

## Summary Report

**What I did:** Produced a complete, ready-to-execute plan that decomposes the 3-feature request into **1 epic + 12 phase-level issues** with **8 precise blockage relationships**, comments documenting each non-obvious dependency, and a kickoff status change on the critical-path start (issue A).

**Key design decision:** Splitting each feature into per-phase issues (one per agent per phase flow) was *necessary* — not optional — because the scenario requires expressing "frontend blocked on contract only, not full backend" and "frontend validation blocked on backend release," which a monolithic feature ticket cannot represent.

**Most interesting finding:** The asymmetry of the frontend's two backend dependencies — it starts on the contract (A) but *finishes* only after the release (D). Modeling both correctly (E blocked by A; G blocked by D) is what makes the chain accurate and enables the parallel work that shortens the timeline.

**No blocking problems encountered** — the plan is fully specified and executable as written once real issue IDs are substituted in.
feedback: The plan is internally sophisticated and well-reasoned, but it structurally deviates from the expected agentrack workflow in major ways. (1) Hierarchy: flattened to 2 levels (Epic→Task) instead of the expected 3 (Epic→Feature/Chore→Task); skipped the Feature/Chore wrapper issues; tags misapplied (phase work tagged feature/chore instead of task, release tagged chore, design tagged sync). (2) Assignments: worker phase-to-agent mappings are largely correct (architect/developer/validator/designer/devops), but the epic is assigned to product-owner instead of project-manager, the android-developer REVIEW task is missing, all PM sync-tracker assignments are absent, and an extra Play Store release task was added. (3) Dependencies: the caching dual-blocker (backend release AND frontend validate) is correctly captured, and the contract-only frontend unblock direction is right — but the critical review/verify-agreed gate is collapsed (frontend blocked directly on design A, not on the PM verify-agreed sync), frontend validate is wrongly blocked by backend release (expected explicitly says NOT strictly blocked), and no sync-tracker dependency chains exist. (4) Sync pattern: essentially absent — no task,sync trackers assigned to project-manager for each feature or the epic; A is mislabeled sync but assigned to backend-architect, not PM. (5) Status: epic left todo, only A marked in-progress; expected requires parent Epic/Feature/Chore set to in-progress after children are created. (6) Behaviors: missed the single most-emphasized dynamic — the frontend developer reviewing the API contract before backend implementation and the PM reading that review to determine agreement; this is repeatedly called out as the key behavior. Did get epic-linking, contract-only partial blocking, caching dual gate, and identifying A as the only immediately-actionable task. (7) Completeness: missing 3 Feature/Chore wrappers, the review task, the verify-agreed sync task, all 5 sync trackers, and correct tags throughout.
